scenes.title: dbt Sources & Seeds
scenes.narration: This lesson covers two ways raw data enters a dbt project: declared sources for warehouse tables and seeds for small CSV files.

scenes.title: What sources give you
bullets: A named handle for raw loaded tables
Freshness checks on when data last arrived
Lineage that starts at the true origin
scenes.narration: A source is a declaration that tells dbt about the raw tables an ingestion tool has already loaded. Declaring sources gives you a clean named handle instead of hard-coded schema names, lets dbt run freshness checks to warn when data has gone stale, and ensures your lineage graph begins at the true origin of the data.

scenes.title: Declaring a source
scenes.code:
# models/staging/_sources.yml
sources:
  - name: jaffle_shop
    schema: raw
    freshness:
      warn_after: {count: 12, period: hour}
    tables:
      - name: orders
      - name: customers
scenes.narration: This YAML declares a source group called jaffle_shop that points at the raw schema. The freshness block asks dbt to warn if the newest record is more than twelve hours old, which is a cheap early-warning system for broken upstream loads. Under tables we list the individual raw tables so dbt knows they exist and can track them in lineage.

scenes.title: Referencing a source in a model
scenes.code:
-- models/staging/stg_orders.sql
select
    id as order_id,
    customer_id,
    order_date
from {{ source('jaffle_shop', 'orders') }}
scenes.narration: In a model you point at a declared source using the source function with the group name and the table name. dbt resolves this to the fully qualified raw table at build time, so if the underlying schema ever changes you update it in one place. Using the source function rather than a hard-coded name is what wires the raw table into dbt's dependency graph.

scenes.title: Sources versus Seeds

right.heading: seed
points: Small CSV committed to the repo

scenes.narration: Sources and seeds solve different problems. A source references large, changing raw tables that some other tool loaded, and dbt only reads from them. A seed is a small static CSV you commit directly into the repository, which dbt itself loads into the warehouse with the dbt seed command. Seeds shine for tiny lookup tables like country-code mappings that rarely change.

scenes.text: Always read raw data through source() and never hard-code raw schema names, so lineage and freshness stay intact.
scenes.narration: The habit to build is always reading raw data through the source function rather than hard-coding schema names, because that is what keeps your lineage graph complete and your freshness checks meaningful.
